sources.entry: RSS Monster - Easy to use web-based RSS aggregator and reader compatible with the Fever API (alternative to Google Reader). MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: RSSMonster is a self-hosted, web-based RSS reader and aggregator with optional semantic organization, compatible with the Fever and Google Reader APIs.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a web reader with Reader, Expanded, and Summarized modes, bookmarks, read-state control, keyboard shortcuts, and light/dark themes. Subscriptions can be arranged into categories, articles tagged, and regex-based actions can bookmark, mark read, tag, hide, or override scores on incoming articles. Search combines words, dates, state, and tags, and queries can be saved as Smart Folders. Optional inference adds event grouping of related coverage, interest-based recommendations, article quality and source-trust scoring, and an OpenAI-backed assistant. Users can import and export OPML and expose saved selections as tokenized generated RSS feeds. Fever and Google Reader API compatibility supports external client apps.
use_cases: Organizing feeds into categories and tags
Filtering feeds with regex rules and saved searches
Following multiple reports about the same story
Reading RSS in third-party Fever or Google Reader clients
how_to_run: Generate two random secrets with: openssl rand -hex 32
Add JWT_SECRET and FEVER_CREDENTIAL_SECRET (different values) to .env
Open the web app and create the first account (it becomes the administrator)
notable: Three deployment tiers: Electron desktop app, SQLite quick start, and a MySQL 8.4 profile with crawl and AI workers
Semantic Events group reports about the same occurrence and separate syndicated copies from independent reporting
Declarative Smart Folders built from advanced search expressions
Fever and Google Reader API compatibility
Progressive Web App support with optional Web Push
caveats: MariaDB is currently blocked for the 2.4 migration runner; only MySQL 8.4 and SQLite are supported for migrations
The Electron desktop app has no scheduled crawling and requires manual feed refresh
The assistant requires an OpenAI provider; advanced inference features need extra setup such as model downloads and worker processes
